scenarios.title: Runbook from a control-plane incident
scenarios.prompt: Turn our incident notes into a runbook for next time: 'VM creation failed, existing VMs OK. RabbitMQ RPC broken, Galera unhealthy. We stopped the APIs (pulled them from HAProxy), purged RabbitMQ queues and restarted the RabbitMQ cluster, then restarted MariaDB. Checked Galera size/Primary, rabbit cluster + consumers, compute services and agents up, test VM create/ping/delete. Reopened APIs. Root cause later: RabbitMQ network partition.'
available_evidence: incident notes describing the sequence and verification (provided)
root cause was a RabbitMQ partition (provided)
missing_information: exact commands and environment (deployment tool, containerization)
versions, queue types, partition handling setting
how to identify the most advanced Galera node if a bootstrap is needed
expected_reasoning: scopes the runbook to the failure mode and lists what it does not cover
adds decision points: RabbitMQ node-left vs partition; Galera single node vs quorum loss
makes stopping the APIs a decision requiring an authorized owner, with communication
keeps queue purge as an explicit decision stating the loss of in-flight operations
includes must-not-do items (reset nodes during partition before escalation; bootstrap wrong Galera node)
keeps the verification list as end-to-end checks
marks unknown commands as TODOs instead of inventing them
marks the runbook as draft pending validation by a non-author
expected_output: runbook following the template with decision points, steps labelled, stop/escalate, must-not-do, verification, recovery, owner, validation plan, author notes
critical_errors: turns the incident sequence into an unconditional procedure (always purge and restart)
invents environment-specific commands or hostnames as fact
criteria: Includes decision points distinguishing partition from node loss
Gates stopping APIs and purging queues behind an authorized decision
Marks missing details as TODOs rather than inventing them
Includes owner, validation plan by a non-author, and draft status
Records why steps exist (reasoning), not only commands

scenarios.title: Review a thin existing runbook
scenarios.prompt: Please review our runbook 'RabbitMQ alarm': 1) restart rabbitmq-server on all three nodes 2) restart all nova and neutron services 3) check that the alarm cleared.
missing_information: alarm types it is meant for (memory, disk, partition, node down)
expected_reasoning: identifies missing purpose/scope: one runbook for many different alarms
no decision points: same alert can mean node left, partition, memory/disk alarm
restarting all nodes at once is high blast radius and may lose queues; restarting all services causes reconnect storms
verification checks the alarm, not the capability
no stop/escalation, no must-not-do, no owner, no validation date, no reasoning
provides a findings table before any rewrite
expected_output: findings table, then a restructured draft with decision points and TODOs
critical_errors: rewrites it while keeping 'restart all nodes' as an unconditional first step
criteria: Points out missing scope and decision points for different alarm types
Flags simultaneous restart of all nodes/services as dangerous
Flags verification of the alarm rather than the capability
Flags missing stop/escalation, owner and validation
Gives findings before a rewritten version

scenarios.title: Capture Galera full-outage recovery from a leaving expert's notes
scenarios.prompt: Our DB expert leaves Friday. His notes on Galera full outage recovery say only: 'find node with highest seqno, bootstrap it, start the others'. Can you turn this into a proper runbook?
available_evidence: brief notes on Galera full-outage recovery (provided)
expected_reasoning: adds the grastate.dat seqno and safe_to_bootstrap check, and --wsrep-recover after unclean shutdown when seqno is -1
warns that bootstrapping the wrong node discards committed transactions (must-not-do)
adds preconditions: confirm it is a full outage, not a single-node failure (decision point)
adds verification: cluster size, Primary state, services writing, capability check
marks environment-specific commands as TODOs
proposes validation by someone else before Friday, observed by the expert
expected_output: runbook draft with decision points, steps, must-not-do, verification, validation plan using the expert's remaining days
critical_errors: omits the safe_to_bootstrap / wsrep-recover identification step
presents invented service names or paths as fact
does not propose a validation session before the expert leaves
criteria: Includes identification of the most advanced node (seqno, safe_to_bootstrap, wsrep-recover)
States the data-loss risk of bootstrapping the wrong node as must-not-do or stop condition
Adds a decision point distinguishing full outage from partial failure
Proposes validation by a non-author while the expert is still available
